title: Session-Scoped Retention Governor and Evidence Manifest for Interactive Requests
creator: Ava Li
description: Deliver a session-scoped retention governance model and an evidence manifest export that lets customers define TTLs for interactive artifacts (prompts, responses, per-request logs, and derived metrics) at session, route and tenant levels. The governor should support enforced TTLs, sampled archival, just-in-time evidence stamping, and cryptographically verifiable manifests to satisfy audits. This initiative aims to reduce legal friction for regulated customers while preserving operator controls for cost and reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Policy model: customers can define retention policies scoped to session, route, or tenant with precedence rules (session > route > tenant > default)
TTL enforcement: requests and their associated artifacts are automatically purged or moved to cold storage according to configured TTLs without manual intervention
Evidence manifest: exported bundles include SHA-256 hashes of each artifact, sequence numbers, timestamps, and a signed manifest (KMS-compatible) suitable for audit ingestion
Export API: customers can request evidence bundles for a session or time-range; exports respect residency and export controls and produce a signed, tamper-evident archive
Sampling: sampling rules available to create retained samples for long TTLs to reduce cost; sampling preserves representativeness via stratified session keys
Console UX: retention rules and effective TTLs visible in Console per-route and per-session; preview mode illustrates what would be purged for a given date
Automated alerts: retention drift detection and automated evidence snapshot alerts when policies change or when a large purge job is scheduled
Compatibility: works for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments with same policy semantics and an optional offline evidence export workflow for air-gapped deployments
implementation_notes: Introduce new policy schema with fields: scope, ttl_seconds, sampling_rate, retention_action (purge|archive), residency_constraint, justification_required
Leverage existing snapshotter (ENG-22456) with extension to produce hashed manifests and KMS-signing support (HSM/KMS interfaces)
Add a session-level metadata envelope to request artifacts that captures session_id, route_id, tenant_id, created_at, and lineage pointers for derived metrics
Batch purge pipeline to run incremental deletions with backoff and observability hooks; include safe-guards to prevent accidental tenant-wide deletes
Console: retention preview UI that simulates purge result; API to preview and dry-run exports
Provide CLI and API primitives for evidence download with role-based access controls and audit log entries
Private deployments: document offline export process and encrypted manifest transfer mechanisms for legal teams
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental permanent deletion affecting production debugging. Mitigation: require canary/pilot flag and enforce a safety window + confirmation for first tenant-level rule; retention preview and dry-run required before enforcement
Risk: large purge jobs spike load and cost. Mitigation: throttled background workers, prioritized by tenant SLAs, and quota-backed purge throttling
Risk: evidence exports leak PII. Mitigation: residency constraints, export allowlists, and per-export access control checks with audit logging
Risk: signature key compromise. Mitigation: rotate signing keys, publish verification endpoints, require KMS/HSM usage for enterprise customers
